text: You fake it, you do a fake door test, you do a smoke test, Wizard of Oz tests.
speaker: Itamar Gilad
context: Lenny asks Itamar about methods for testing product ideas before building them. Itamar explains various low-cost validation techniques including fake door tests, smoke tests, and Wizard of Oz tests - methods where you simulate a working product without actually building the real functionality. He shares how his team at Google used this approach when developing Gmail's tabbed inbox feature, creating an HTML facade that manually sorted messages to test user reactions before writing any actual code.
text_ko: 일단 되는 척해요. 페이크 도어 테스트(fake door test), 스모크 테스트(smoke test), 위자드 오브 오즈 테스트(Wizard of Oz tests) 같은 걸 해 봐요.
text_zh: 你就是先做做样子，跑个门面测试 (fake door test)、冒烟测试 (smoke test)，或者奥兹魔法师测试 (Wizard of Oz tests)。
text_es: Simulas: haces una prueba de puerta falsa (fake door test), un smoke test (smoke test) y pruebas Wizard of Oz (Wizard of Oz tests).
key_sentence: You fake it, you do a fake door test, you do a smoke test, Wizard of Oz tests.
original_text: You fake it, you do a fake door test, you do a smoke test, Wizard of Oz tests. We used a lot of those in the tabbed inbox by the way, one of the first early versions was actually we showed the tabbed inbox working to people. But it wasn't really Gmail, it was just a facade of HTML and behind the scenes and according to the permissions that the users gave us some of us moved just the subject and the sender into the right place.

text: Google+ was my first experience at Gmail, I joined Gmail in August 2011 and the first thing they asked me is, "Let's connect Gmail with Google+." If you're hazy about the story, back then Facebook was massive.
speaker: Itamar Gilad
context: Lenny asks Itamar to share the story of his work on Google+ and Gmail that shaped his product development philosophy. Itamar explains that when he joined Gmail in 2011, his first assignment was integrating Gmail with Google+, Google's new social network created in response to Facebook's rapid growth. He describes how Facebook's success 'freaked out' Google leadership, leading them to launch their own social platform that initially seemed promising within the company.
text_ko: 구글 플러스(Google+)가 지메일(Gmail)에서의 첫 경험이었어요. 저는 2011년 8월에 지메일에 합류했는데, 제일 먼저 들은 말이 "지메일을 구글 플러스와 연결해보자"였어요. 혹시 그 이야기가 잘 떠오르지 않으면, 그때는 페이스북(Facebook)이 정말 대세였어요.
text_zh: 我在Gmail的第一项工作就是跟Google+打交道。2011年8月我进了Gmail团队，刚来人他们就跟我说：“把Gmail和Google+对接起来吧。”要是你对当时情况有点模糊，那会儿Facebook正火得不得了。
text_es: Mi primera experiencia en Gmail fue con Google+. Llegué a Gmail en agosto de 2011 y lo primero que me pidieron fue: "conectemos Gmail con Google+". Si no lo recuerdas bien, por aquel entonces Facebook estaba en pleno auge.
original_text: Google+ was my first experience at Gmail, I joined Gmail in August 2011 and the first thing they asked me is, "Let's connect Gmail with Google+." If you're hazy about the story, back then Facebook was massive. It's still massive but then it was growing like mushrooms, people were spending hours. That really freaked out Google and the obvious solution was to launch a social network of Google called Google+ and we all believe in this thing, it really caught on very well initially we all used it, we all believed in it.

vocabulary.definition: Extremely large or heavy; significant in size or impact.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, 'massive' often describes substantial market trends, large-scale operations, or significant investments that can influence industry dynamics.
vocabulary.nuance: The term conveys not only size but also importance, and should be used when emphasizing the scale of an impact or presence.

vocabulary.definition: The knowledge or skill acquired through practical involvement in a particular activity or field.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, 'experience' often refers to an individual's background and expertise, which can be critical for hiring decisions and project management.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'experience' generally has a positive connotation, it can also imply a lack of innovation if one relies solely on past knowledge without adapting to new trends.

text: So putting aside all the tremendous waste that went into this, all the millions of person hours and personal weeks. In hindsight, not only did Google bet on the wrong thing it missed much easier opportunities.
speaker: Itamar Gilad
context: Lenny asks about the scale of resources invested in the Google+ project. Itamar reflects on the massive waste of resources - millions of person hours - that Google+ represented when it ultimately failed. He points out the irony that while Google was building a Facebook competitor, WhatsApp (located near Google's headquarters) was creating a much more successful social product that actually threatened Facebook, representing the kind of opportunity Google missed by focusing on the wrong approach.
text_zh: 撇开这件事上投入的巨大浪费不谈——数百万工时，很多人都牺牲了好几周的时间。事后看来，谷歌不仅押错了注，还错过了很多更容易抓住的机会。
text_es: Si dejamos a un lado todo el tremendo despilfarro que hubo aquí —los millones de horas-persona (person hours) y las semanas-persona (person-weeks) que se invirtieron—, en retrospectiva Google no solo apostó por la opción equivocada, sino que además dejó pasar oportunidades mucho más sencillas.
key_sentence: Google bet on the wrong thing, missing easier opportunities not far from headquarters.
original_text: So putting aside all the tremendous waste that went into this, all the millions of person hours and personal weeks. In hindsight, not only did Google bet on the wrong thing it missed much easier opportunities. So just not far from Google's headquarters there was WhatsApp, not very famous in the US but they actually created massive impact. Hundreds of millions of people were using their stuff and they became a threat to Facebook much more than Google was.

vocabulary.definition: Extremely large in amount, scale, or intensity; remarkable.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'tremendous' is often used to describe significant achievements, challenges, or impacts that can affect an organization's performance or reputation.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'tremendous' generally conveys a positive connotation, it can also imply a negative aspect when referring to waste or loss.

vocabulary.definition: Understanding a situation or event only after it has happened, often with the benefit of knowledge gained from the outcome.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business analysis, hindsight is crucial for evaluating past decisions and strategies to inform future planning and risk management.
vocabulary.nuance: Using 'hindsight' often implies a critical reflection that suggests better decisions could have been made with the knowledge available after the fact.

vocabulary.definition: Situations or conditions favorable for achieving a goal or making progress.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups and business development, identifying and leveraging opportunities is essential for growth and competitive advantage.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'opportunities' carries a positive connotation and suggests potential for success, but it can also imply risks if not pursued wisely.

text: So for me, this story kind of was the epitome of what I call today, opinion-based development. We come up with an idea, we believe in it, all the indications show it's good.
speaker: Itamar Gilad
context: Lenny asks Itamar about lessons learned from the Google+ experience. Itamar explains how Google+ became the perfect example of 'opinion-based development' - a flawed approach where teams become overly confident in their ideas based on limited evidence and then commit massive resources without proper validation. He admits his own role in perpetuating this mistake as a product manager who enthusiastically championed ideas without sufficient evidence.
text_ko: 저한테 이 이야기는 요즘 제가 '의견 기반 개발(opinion-based development)'이라고 부르는 방식의 전형이었어요. 아이디어를 내고 그걸 믿으면, 모든 지표가 괜찮다고 나오니까요.
text_zh: 对我来说，这件事可以说就是我现在所说的那种“凭主观意见做开发”(opinion-based development)的典型。我们想了个点子，相信它，各种迹象看起来都在支持它。
text_es: Para mí, esta historia fue, en cierto modo, el claro ejemplo de lo que hoy llamo desarrollo basado en opiniones (opinion-based development). Se nos ocurre una idea, creemos en ella y todo indica que va a funcionar.
key_sentence: this story kind of was the epitome of what I call today, opinion-based development.
original_text: So for me, this story kind of was the epitome of what I call today, opinion-based development. We come up with an idea, we believe in it, all the indications show it's good. Maybe the early tests show it's good, then we just go all in and we try to implement it and I made this very mistake many times as the product manager, I was the guy pushing for the ideas.

vocabulary.definition: A person or thing that is a perfect example of a particular quality or type.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'epitome' is often used to describe a model company or product that embodies the best practices or characteristics of a successful category.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'epitome' conveys excellence, it can also imply that something is overly idealized or not representative of the broader context.

vocabulary.definition: A process of creating products or services primarily driven by subjective beliefs rather than empirical evidence or market research.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups, opinion-based development can lead to innovations that may not align with actual customer needs, risking resource misallocation.
vocabulary.nuance: This term often carries a negative connotation, suggesting a lack of rigor in decision-making and reliance on personal biases.

vocabulary.definition: Signs or pieces of information that suggest something may be true or likely to happen.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, indications can refer to market trends, customer feedback, or performance metrics that inform strategic decisions.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'indications' can provide valuable insights, they should be interpreted cautiously, as they may not always predict outcomes accurately.

text: So that sent us, kind of me and my team into researching these users into establishing a goal that was much more user-centric and then thinking of other ideas.
speaker: Itamar Gilad
context: Lenny asks about the contrasting approach used for Gmail's tabbed inbox feature. Itamar describes how skeptical feedback from colleagues forced his team to adopt a more evidence-based approach. Instead of immediately building their idea, they researched users more deeply, established user-centric goals, and implemented rigorous testing methods - starting with their own inboxes, then expanding to other Google employees (called 'dog fooders' in tech parlance), and finally external users.
text_ko: 그 계기로 저와 제 팀은 그 사용자들을 더 조사(user research)하게 됐고, 훨씬 사용자 중심(user-centric)인 목표(goal)를 세우게 됐어요. 그 다음에 다른 아이디어들도 생각해봤어요.
text_zh: 于是我和团队就去研究这些用户，确定了一个更以用户为中心(user-centric)的目标，然后开始想其他的点子。
text_es: Eso hizo que mi equipo y yo empezáramos a investigar a estos usuarios, a fijar un objetivo mucho más centrado en el usuario (user-centric) y a pensar en nuevas ideas.
key_sentence: establishing a goal that was much more user-centric
original_text: So that sent us, kind of me and my team into researching these users into establishing a goal that was much more user-centric and then thinking of other ideas. And then we started testing them much more rigorously and basically we started testing on our own inboxes and then we recruited other dog footers, other Googlers to test the same inbox, then we put it outside for external testers.

vocabulary.definition: Focused on the needs, preferences, and experiences of the end user in the design and development of products or services.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, a user-centric approach is essential for creating products that effectively meet customer demands and enhance user satisfaction.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'user-centric' emphasizes empathy and understanding of users, it should not overshadow other important business considerations like profitability and scalability.

vocabulary.definition: The process of setting up, creating, or formalizing something, such as a goal, system, or relationship.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, establishing clear objectives and frameworks is crucial for guiding teams and ensuring alignment with strategic goals.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often implies a foundational or initial phase, and should be used when referring to the creation of something new rather than ongoing processes.

vocabulary.definition: The systematic investigation into and study of materials and sources to establish facts and reach new conclusions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, researching is vital for understanding market trends, consumer behavior, and competitive landscapes, thereby informing strategic decisions.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'researching' implies a thorough and methodical approach, it should be distinguished from casual inquiry or superficial investigation.

text: I think the founders are very important, especially in the startup and scale-ups phase. They come up with many of the most important ideas and it's super important that they have the space to express and to push the organization to look at those.
speaker: Itamar Gilad
context: Lenny asks whether there are instances where opinion-based approaches make sense, particularly with visionary founders like Steve Jobs. Itamar clarifies that founders play a crucial role in generating important ideas, especially in startups and scale-ups, and should have space to express their vision. However, he emphasizes that the solution isn't to shut down founder ideas but rather to examine them critically with evidence rather than blindly executing them.
text_ko: 저는 창업자(founders)들이 특히 스타트업과 스케일업 단계(startup and scale-ups phase)에서 정말 중요하다고 생각해요. 많은 핵심 아이디어들이 그들로부터 나오기 때문에, 그런 아이디어를 자유롭게 표현하고 조직이 주목해서 검토하도록 밀어붙일 수 있는 여지가 있는 게 정말 중요해요.
text_zh: 我觉得创始人 (founders) 非常重要，尤其在创业和规模化阶段 (startup and scale-ups phase)。他们常常会想出很多关键的想法，所以一定要给他们足够的空间去表达，并推动组织去考虑这些想法。
text_es: Creo que los fundadores son fundamentales, sobre todo en la fase de startups y scale-ups (startup and scale-ups). Suelen tener muchas de las ideas más importantes, y es vital que tengan espacio para expresarlas y para empujar a la organización a que las tenga en cuenta.
key_sentence: Founders are crucial in the scale-ups phase, pushing the organization to look critically.
original_text: I think the founders are very important, especially in the startup and scale-ups phase. They come up with many of the most important ideas and it's super important that they have the space to express and to push the organization to look at those. However, it's not about shutting them down it's about looking at them critically.

vocabulary.definition: Individuals who establish a company or organization, often taking on significant risk and responsibility in its early stages.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups, founders are crucial as they drive the initial vision, culture, and strategy of the business.
vocabulary.nuance: The term carries a connotation of innovation and entrepreneurship, often implying a strong personal investment in the company's success.

vocabulary.definition: A newly established business, typically in the early stages of development and often focused on innovative products or services.
vocabulary.businessContext: Startups are characterized by their potential for rapid growth and are often funded by venture capital or angel investors seeking high returns.
vocabulary.nuance: The term suggests a dynamic and often uncertain environment, where agility and adaptability are essential for survival.

vocabulary.definition: Businesses that have moved beyond the startup phase and are experiencing significant growth, often expanding their operations and market reach.
vocabulary.businessContext: Scale-ups are critical in the business ecosystem as they contribute to job creation and economic development by leveraging their established models for larger impact.
vocabulary.nuance: The term implies a transition from survival to sustainability, emphasizing the importance of strategic planning and resource management.

text: I think there's a few telltale signs that I look for, first the goals are very unclear. Either there are many or they're very kind of obscure and vague or they are about output, there's misalignment.
speaker: Itamar Gilad
context: Lenny asks what signs indicate that a company isn't as evidence-guided as they think they are. Itamar identifies several telltale signs of poor evidence-guided practices: unclear, numerous, or vague goals that focus on outputs rather than outcomes, misalignment across teams, and inadequate metrics - particularly the absence of user-facing metrics while only tracking business metrics like revenue.
text_ko: 제가 주로 보는 몇 가지 뚜렷한 징후가 있어요. 첫째, 목표가 아주 불명확해요 — 목표가 너무 많거나 애매모호하거나, 혹은 산출물(output)에만 치우쳐 있으면 전체적으로 정렬이 안 돼서 불일치(misalignment)가 생겨요.
text_zh: 我通常会留意几条明显的信号。第一，目标很不清楚：要么目标太多、抓不住重点；要么说得很模糊；要么只盯着产出(output)，结果大家方向不一致(misalignment)。
text_es: Creo que hay algunas señales claras que suelo buscar: primero, los objetivos están muy poco claros. O hay demasiados, o son poco concretos y vagos, o están centrados en los resultados (output) y hay falta de alineación.
key_sentence: Unclear goals are telltale signs, often obscure and vague, lacking user facing metrics.
original_text: I think there's a few telltale signs that I look for, first the goals are very unclear. Either there are many or they're very kind of obscure and vague or they are about output, there's misalignment. So the goals part is not there, usually this goes hand in hand with metrics. Missing metrics or just using revenue and business metric but there's no user facing metrics.

vocabulary.definition: Indicators or clues that reveal the presence of a particular situation or condition.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, telltale signs can help managers identify potential issues or opportunities, such as employee dissatisfaction or market trends.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase often implies that the signs are subtle yet significant, and should be interpreted carefully to avoid misjudgment.

vocabulary.definition: A lack of agreement or alignment between different elements, such as goals, strategies, or teams.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a corporate environment, misalignment can lead to inefficiencies, confusion, and failure to achieve objectives, making it crucial to address early.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often carries a negative connotation, suggesting that corrective action is needed to realign efforts and resources.

vocabulary.definition: Not easily understood or lacking in clarity; ambiguous.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business communications, unclear messages can lead to misunderstandings and hinder effective collaboration among teams.
vocabulary.nuance: While it can describe any lack of clarity, in a business context, it often suggests a need for more precise communication or defined objectives.

vocabulary.definition: Not clearly expressed or defined; lacking specific details.
vocabulary.businessContext: Vague objectives or instructions in a business setting can result in confusion and misinterpretation, impacting project outcomes.
vocabulary.nuance: This term often implies a need for more specificity and can suggest that the speaker is avoiding directness or clarity.
